title: Post-Incident Review: P1 Mumbai Core Outage and P2 Recurrence (INC-0001, INC-0002)
body:
## Executive Summary
On 14 November 2024, Aarohan Digital Networks experienced a P1 complete service outage in the Mumbai Metropolitan Circle affecting 380,000 subscribers for 5 hours 38 minutes. A follow-up P2 recurrence on 2 December confirmed the initial corrective action (ECMP policy rollback) addressed the wrong root cause.

## Timeline of Events
- 02:14 IST 14-Nov: NOC alarms for Mumbai Circle — subscriber count drops to zero.
- 02:31 IST: P1 declared. War room convened with NOC Lead, Network Architect, and Circle Operations Manager.
- 03:45 IST: ECMP hypothesis confirmed by NOC. Rollback initiated on 3 of 7 chassis.
- 07:52 IST: Services restored after partial chassis restart. ECMP rollback credited as resolution.
- 22-Nov: Juniper TAC confirms firmware defect. ECMP hypothesis invalidated.
- 2-Dec: P2 recurrence. Firmware upgraded to 21.4R3-S4. No further recurrence as of report date.

## Root Cause
Juniper MX480 firmware 21.4R3-S2 contains a defect in MPLS label stack processing that manifests under sustained traffic loads above 18 Gbps. The initial mis-diagnosis cost an estimated 90 minutes of additional downtime and made the first corrective action entirely ineffective, directly causing the recurrence.

## Corrective Actions
- ACT-0001 (completed, ineffective) — ECMP rollback — did not address root cause
- Emergency firmware upgrade to 21.4R3-S4 across all MX480 chassis (prevented recurrence)

## Recommendations
1. All MX480 chassis running 21.4R3-S2 or earlier must be upgraded to 21.4R3-S4 within 30 days.
2. The ECMP policy change process must include a 24-hour traffic soak test before production deployment.
3. Incident response runbooks must include a firmware version verification step in the triage checklist.

title: Corrective Action Tracker — NSA Architecture Decision (DEC-0001) — 5G Phase 2
body:
## Corrective Action Tracker

### Background
This CAT was raised following the negative outcome of decision DEC-0001 — adoption of NSA 5G architecture for the Phase 2 core rollout. The decision led to the 5G Core Network Upgrade Phase 2 project being placed on hold with 3 of 4 milestones delayed or incomplete.

### Actions Tracked
| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status | Effectiveness |
|--------|-------|----------|--------|---------------|
| ACT-0002 | Architecture Team | 60 days from issue | In Progress | TBD |
| ACT-0003 | Finance + NOC | 30 days from issue | In Progress | TBD |
| ACT-0004 | CISO + CTO | 30 days from issue | In Progress | TBD |

### Closure Criteria
Each action is closed when the assigned owner submits evidence of completion and the sponsoring executive signs off. The CAT will be marked complete when all three actions are closed and a final review confirms the root causes have been addressed.

### Escalation
Any action overdue by more than 14 days is automatically escalated to the CISO and CTO for review at the next Architecture Review Board meeting.

title: Post-Incident Review — P1 Core Network Outage — Mumbai Metro Ci (INC-0001)
body:
## Post-Incident Review

### Executive Summary
This PIR documents the timeline, root cause, impact, and corrective actions following the incident.

### Timeline of Events
- NOC detected service degradation via automated alarm correlation
- Incident escalated to P1/P2 after subscriber impact confirmed
- War room convened with NOC Lead, Network Architect, and Circle Operations Manager
- Service restoration completed after root cause was identified and remediated

### Root Cause
The confirmed root cause is documented in the incident record. Initial diagnosis differed from the confirmed cause, leading to additional investigation time.

### Corrective Actions
All corrective actions raised from this incident are tracked in the linked ACT- records. Progress is reviewed weekly by the incident owner.

### Recommendations
1. Update runbooks to include the new diagnostic steps identified during this incident.
2. Implement automated detection for the specific failure signature observed.
3. Conduct a tabletop exercise with the NOC team to rehearse the revised response procedure.

title: Lessons Learned Report — Optical Transport Layer Expansion — Bengaluru-Mumbai Corridor
body:
## Lessons Learned Report

### Overview
This report captures the key lessons learned from the completed or cancelled project. It is intended to inform future similar initiatives and improve organisational capability.

### What Went Well
- Strong cross-functional collaboration during the delivery phase
- Proactive risk identification led to early mitigation of several threats
- Vendor engagement and contract management were effective

### What Could Be Improved
- Requirements sign-off took longer than planned, compressing the delivery timeline
- Change management activities should start earlier in the project lifecycle
- Testing coverage for edge-case scenarios was insufficient

### Recommendations for Future Projects
1. Include a dedicated change management workstream from project initiation.
2. Mandate independent architecture review for all projects with cross-circle impact.
3. Build in a minimum 10% schedule contingency for complex integration work.

title: Root Cause Analysis Report — P1 Core Network Outage — Mumbai Metro Circle
body:
## Root Cause Analysis Report

### Background
This RCA report was commissioned following a significant operational event. It provides a structured analysis of the contributing factors and root cause.

### 5-Whys Analysis
1. Why did the service fail? — A hardware or software fault triggered a service interruption.
2. Why was the fault not detected earlier? — Monitoring thresholds were not calibrated for this failure mode.
3. Why were thresholds not calibrated? — No baseline had been established for this specific metric.
4. Why was no baseline established? — The system was newly deployed without a formal commissioning checklist.
5. Why was no commissioning checklist used? — The checklist was not updated to include this system type.

### Contributing Factors
- Incomplete monitoring coverage
- Process gap in change management
- Insufficient runbook coverage for this failure scenario

### Corrective Actions
Corrective actions have been raised and are tracked in the linked ACT- records.
